To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
expression of LDL-A module in prostate cancer cells suppresses prostate cancer growth in vitro and in xenografts.
expression of LDL-A module in prostate cancer cells inhibited prostate tumor growth in vivo and decreased tumor cell growth, invasion, and metastasis in vitro.
overexpression of LDL-A inhibits prostate tumorigenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of the LDL-A module in the relaxin receptor and the effects of this expression on prostate cancer cell growth.
the role of RXFP1-Low Density Lipoprotein-A module in prostate tumorigenesis.
the expression and function of the RXFP1 receptor and its potential as a novel therapeutic target for prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LDL-A module inhibits prostate cancer progression.
expression of the LDL-A module in PC3 cells inhibits prostate cancer growth and progression.
the inhibition of relaxin-RXFP1 signaling by the LDL-A module can inhibit prostate cancer progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LDL-A peptide is an antagonist for the relaxin receptor, which inhibits prostate cancer growth and progression.
the LDL-A module can be used to block relaxin signaling in prostate cancer cells and suppress prostate cancer progression.

we have demonstrated that the LDL-A module can be used for the inhibition of relaxin signaling in prostate cancer cells and that this inhibition is mediated by a reduction in Akt phosphorylation and the downregulation of MMP2 and several other genes involved in prostate cancer progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LDL-A module can inhibit the relaxin signaling in cancer cells.
the LDL-A module can be used to inhibit the activity of relaxin receptors, and thus inhibit prostate cancer cell proliferation, migration and invasion.
the LDL-A module is a potential inhibitor of prostate cancer progression.
